title: AlphaGenome scripts pass a 0-based position to genome.Variant, which expects 1-based
body:
Hi Marcel,

Thanks for publishing the code and per-variant calls. While writing up your preprint I think I found an off-by-one in both AlphaGenome scripts. It would explain part of AlphaGenome's low sensitivity on the 65-gene set.

## The problem

Both scripts convert the variant position to 0-based and pass that to `genome.Variant`:

- [`2c8_alphagenome_splicescorer.py` line 98](https://github.com/marcel-2c8/Probing-genomic-foundation-models-2026/blob/3c0c6cc327ad8ad75991c71888aef21277917ca9/models/2_alphagenome/2c8_alphagenome_splicescorer.py#L98) and [line 120](https://github.com/marcel-2c8/Probing-genomic-foundation-models-2026/blob/3c0c6cc327ad8ad75991c71888aef21277917ca9/models/2_alphagenome/2c8_alphagenome_splicescorer.py#L120)
- [`2c8_alphagenome_junctionscorer.py` line 89](https://github.com/marcel-2c8/Probing-genomic-foundation-models-2026/blob/3c0c6cc327ad8ad75991c71888aef21277917ca9/models/2_alphagenome/2c8_alphagenome_junctionscorer.py#L89) and [line 110](https://github.com/marcel-2c8/Probing-genomic-foundation-models-2026/blob/3c0c6cc327ad8ad75991c71888aef21277917ca9/models/2_alphagenome/2c8_alphagenome_junctionscorer.py#L110)

```python
target_pos = pos_1based - 1                # convert to 0-based
...
variant = genome.Variant(chromosome=chrom, position=target_pos, reference_bases=ref_csv, alternate_bases=alt_csv)
```

AlphaGenome's `Variant.position` is 1-based ([`genome.py` line 656](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphagenome/blob/55943112b83439e0c2512110f1ae607d4b5b492a/src/alphagenome/data/genome.py#L656): "The 1-based position of the variant on the chromosome"; `start` is `position - 1`). The client does not check `reference_bases` against the genome. So each variant is applied one base to the left of the real variant.

The UCSC reference check runs at the correct base, so it passes. The `Interval` and the ±500 bp slice are centred on the true position, so only the edit is misplaced. The SpliceAI, Borzoi and NTv3 scripts handle coordinates correctly; only the AlphaGenome scripts are affected.

## Check against Supplementary Table VI

For each positive in the 65-gene set I fetched hg38 bases around the variant (UCSC API, same as your scripts) and worked out which transcript position AlphaGenome actually edited: one base upstream for plus-strand genes, one base downstream for minus-strand genes. I then compared that with the calls in Supplementary Table VI. All 183 REF bases matched hg38 at the true position. I count 75 unique positives after de-duplicating; your table says 76, so one may be lost in my join.

| Base AlphaGenome actually edited | AlphaGenome splice scorer | SpliceAI |
|---|---|---|
| A canonical ±1/±2 base (n=20) | 14/20 | 18/20 |
| Not a canonical ±1/±2 base (n=55) | 17/55 | 48/55 |
| Fisher exact test | OR 5.2, p = 0.003 | OR 1.3, p = 1.0 |

AlphaGenome's calls follow the shifted edit; SpliceAI's do not. The clearest group is c.N-1G acceptor variants in minus-strand genes, where the shift moves the edit into the exon. AlphaGenome's splice scorer flags none of the six (COL6A3, ABCA12, TTN, CHD8, EMC1, ATP1A3); SpliceAI flags all six.

This is indirect evidence. A rerun with `position=pos_1based` would show the real effect. The thresholds (0.14 and 0.43) were tuned on OPA1 scores made with the same shift, so they would need re-tuning too.

## Smaller points, in case they are useful

- [`TRACK_NAMES`](https://github.com/marcel-2c8/Probing-genomic-foundation-models-2026/blob/3c0c6cc327ad8ad75991c71888aef21277917ca9/models/2_alphagenome/2c8_alphagenome_splicescorer.py#L78) labels the four SPLICE_SITES tracks "Acceptor, Donor, ExonBody, Intron". Per the [AlphaGenome metadata docs](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphagenome/blob/55943112b83439e0c2512110f1ae607d4b5b492a/docs/source/exploring_model_metadata.md), they are donor and acceptor on the positive and negative strands. The max over all four doesn't change, but the methods text ("acceptor, donor, intronic, and exonic sites") follows the script's labels.
- The `GeneMaskSplicingScorer` created at [line 70](https://github.com/marcel-2c8/Probing-genomic-foundation-models-2026/blob/3c0c6cc327ad8ad75991c71888aef21277917ca9/models/2_alphagenome/2c8_alphagenome_splicescorer.py#L70) is never used. Deltas are computed from `predict_variant` over all four tracks, including the opposite strand, while the library scorer drops strand-mismatched tracks.
- The junction delta at [line 127](https://github.com/marcel-2c8/Probing-genomic-foundation-models-2026/blob/3c0c6cc327ad8ad75991c71888aef21277917ca9/models/2_alphagenome/2c8_alphagenome_junctionscorer.py#L127) is a raw predicted-count difference. AlphaGenome's junction scorer uses the absolute log-fold change. Raw counts scale with each gene's expression, which may be why the OPA1-tuned 0.43 transfers poorly to other genes.
- The splice-site-usage output, part of the composite splicing score in the AlphaGenome paper, isn't used.

The analysis scripts are short (UCSC fetch, the offset arithmetic and the cross-tab). I'm happy to share them, or to check a rerun if you post one.

Best wishes,
Tim Richardson
